full_judgment:
2. The plaintiffs are the petitioners in this revision case. The plaintiffs case is that land measuring 3.14 decimal comprising CS Khatian No. 43 belonged to Indo Mohon and Monindra Bhusson Saha. Nanda Rani Paul and Nata Kudar Pal became the owners of the suit land along with other land and SA record was prepared accordingly. Naba Kumar was survived by two sons, Radha Shayam and Radha Krishna Pal who owned and possessed the share of Naba Kumar. While Nanda Rani and other co-sharers were in possession of the land they cut and removed thicket and weed and turned the land into arable land and started rearing fish in the pond comprising Plot No. 105 and thus the plaintiffs have been possessing the land. Further case of the plaintiffs is that Nanda Rani Pal and two other co-sharers by deed of gift dated 4-3-77 transferred to Shashi Bala the suit land along with other land and put her in possession. Shahi Bala by registered deed dated 19-8-77 transferred the suit land to the plaintiffs. Thereafter the plaintiffs mutated their names in the revenue record and paid rent. The defendants threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs and they attempted to enter into the suit land and to erect ghar and also catch fish from the pond. 

 3. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement. The defendant's case is that the land measuring 3.14 decimal comprising Khatian No. 51 and land measuring 0.19 decimal comprising Khatian No. 125 belonged to Nanda Rani Pal, Radha Shayan Pal and others, they out of the land measuring 3.14 decimals proposed to sell 2.93 decimals of land comprising the above two Khatians to Abdul Matin Talukder and Abdul Quddus Talukder who wanted to purchase the land and pursuant to that an agreement was entered into on 2-2-65 for selling the land by the said vendors at a consideration of Taka 6,000.00 and the vendors receiving the consideration money executed the bainapatra and delivered possession of the land to the purchaser. Since then the defendants have been in possession of the suit land for inure than 12 years and thereby established their hostile title in the land and they have also erected their dwelling houses on the land and living therein with their family members and the defendants also are rearing fish in the pond and enjoying the land ever since. The defendants' further case is that as the defendants have acquired hostile title in the land defendants Abdul Matin Talukder and Abdul Quddus Talukder being the plaintiffs landed a suit against Nanda Rani Pal and others being Title Suit No. 271 of 1978 for declaration of title which is pending. Shahi Bala being one of the defendants is contesting that suit. Thus the defendants claim is that on the basis of the bainapatra the defendants have been possessing the suit land by erecting their dwelling houses thereon. The defendants denied the deed of gift in the name of Shishai Bala and according to the defendants the deed of gift is fabricated document. 

 4. The learned trial Court dismissed the suit chiefly on the ground that the persons who threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs have not been impleaded as defendants and further found, considering Exts 1 and 2 the, Khatians which contains 3.14 decimals of land in which portion of the entire land the plaintiffs claim their possession is unascertainable and the conclusion of the trial Court is that exclusive possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land has not been proved by the evidence adduced, and the defendants were found to be in possession of the land as they are residing there by constructing their dwelling houses.
